<!-- Generated by codeflower-app's cmd/gendocs: do not edit. -->

Start a sandbox for a project, to work with from VS Code or the browser. Every agent runs in it: Claude Code, Codex, DeepSeek Harness and OpenCode; each chat is one agent's, chosen when it starts.

Each folder is mounted in a subfolder named after it: data folders read-only in /data/input, output folders read-write in /data/output, code folders (your repositories and packages, which the agents may change) read-write in /data/code, and skills folders read-only in /data/skills, where the agents load them from.

With --isolate-network the sandbox has no network of its own: the app is its only way out, and lets it reach only the agents' services and the hosts in the allowlist file. Edit the file while the sandbox runs to allow more.

It prints a link to open in the browser while "codeflower client" runs on your computer, which adds the sandbox there; or, in VS Code, run "code flower: Connect to worker" and paste the codeflower://… line. Sign in to the agents from the page's or VS Code's view of the sandbox; logins are kept in the project. Press Ctrl+C to stop: with no agent working, the sandbox stops at once; otherwise the chats whose agent (or a subagent) works are asked to save their work and wrap up first, and the sandbox stops when they are done, at most after 10 minutes ("client: &#123;wrap_up_minutes: N&#125;" in the config). Ctrl+C twice within 3 seconds stops it at once, and once more while it stops kills it.

Each start saves how the project started in PROJECT.sandbox.yaml next to the project folder: its folders, engine, image, network, port and the key and TLS certificate that its links carry. "codeflower sandbox --continue PROJECT" starts it again with them, on the same port and with the same key, so VS Code and saved page links reconnect; it fails if that port is taken. Flags given with --continue replace the saved settings, or add folders to the saved ones, and are saved for next time. The file is YAML, readable only by you: edit it to change or remove a setting while the sandbox is stopped. --new-key makes the links saved before stop working. Started without --continue, a project still keeps its key and certificate, and its saved port unless --port is given or the port is taken, so VS Code's saved connection still works. See "codeflower projects" to list, copy, move or remove projects.

With --server the sandbox also serves its chat page on the same port and prints a link to it (http://HOST:PORT/?key=…), like Jupyter's: open it in any browser that reaches this machine, e.g. through ssh -L. Anyone with the link controls the agent, and plain HTTP carries the key and the chats unencrypted, so keep job logs private and prefer --host 127.0.0.1 with a tunnel on shared networks.

With --forward-to HOST the app also opens the worker's port on HOST's 127.0.0.1 through a reverse SSH tunnel (ssh -R) while the sandbox runs, so VS Code or the client on HOST connects with the 127.0.0.1 link: for a sandbox on a compute node whose port the login node cannot reach (Docker and Podman publish it on the compute node's 127.0.0.1 only). This node must log in to HOST without a password (an SSH key), and the port must be free there. In a batch job, --forward-to "$SLURM_SUBMIT_HOST" names the node it was submitted from. The tunnel connects again when it drops and stops with the sandbox.

To start a session with an initial task and continue it in VS Code, see "codeflower run". To let the agent work on a task by itself instead, see "codeflower task".


## Usage

```sh
codeflower sandbox [flags]
```

## Examples

```sh
  codeflower sandbox --input ~/data/study42 --output ~/results/study42
  codeflower sandbox --input ~/data/rna --input ~/data/atac --code ~/src/mypkg
  codeflower sandbox --project study42 --input /data/study42
  codeflower sandbox --continue study42
  codeflower sandbox --continue study42 --input ~/data/study42-batch2
  codeflower sandbox --continue study42 --create --input ~/data/study42 --output ~/results/study42
  codeflower sandbox --input ~/data/study42 --skills ~/my-skills --isolate-network
  codeflower sandbox --project study42 --input /data/study42 --forward-to "$SLURM_SUBMIT_HOST"
  codeflower sandbox --image ./codeflower-sandbox.sif --state ~/cf/study42 --bind /data/ref:/reference
```

## Flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--advertise-host string` |  | address printed for VS Code and the page link (default: this node's IPv4 address; 127.0.0.1 with Docker or Podman) |
| `--allowlist string` |  | file of hosts an isolated sandbox may reach, one per line (default: PROJECT.allowed-hosts.txt next to the project) |
| `--bind stringArray` |  | more mounts: SOURCE[:TARGET[:ro\|rw]] (repeatable; default target /data/input/NAME, read-only) |
| `-c, --code stringArray` |  | repository or package the agent develops, mounted read-write at /data/code/NAME (repeatable) |
| `--config string` |  | config directory with config.yaml and skills (or set $CODEFLOWER_CONFIG; default ~/.codeflower) |
| `--continue string` |  | start a project again with its saved settings: a project name, or a project folder (flags given replace settings, or add folders) |
| `--cpus int` |  | CPUs the agent may use (default: the batch job's allocation; Docker and Podman also enforce it) |
| `--create` |  | with --continue: start the project new from the flags given if it does not exist yet (a script can then always use --continue) |
| `--engine string` | `auto` | container engine: auto, docker, podman, or apptainer (or set $CODEFLOWER_ENGINE) |
| `--engine-args stringArray` |  | container engine flags, quoted as one value, e.g. '--gpus all --shm-size 8g': --gpus, --device, --shm-size, --ulimit, --cap-add, --cap-drop, --add-host, --dns (repeatable) |
| `--env stringArray` |  | environment variable for the sandbox: NAME=VALUE, or NAME to take its value from here when the sandbox starts (repeatable) |
| `--env-dir string` |  | folder for what the projects can download or rebuild (software environments, caches, the chats' browsers), e.g. on scratch, in a subfolder per project (or env_dir in the config; default: in the project) |
| `--forward-to HOST` |  | also open the worker's port on HOST's 127.0.0.1 through ssh -R while the sandbox runs, e.g. the login node a compute node's port cannot be reached from (in a batch job: "$SLURM_SUBMIT_HOST") |
| `--host string` | `0.0.0.0` | interface the worker listens on (Apptainer; Docker and Podman always publish on 127.0.0.1) |
| `--image string` |  | sandbox image: a Docker/Podman image name, or an Apptainer .sif file (or set $CODEFLOWER_IMAGE; default ghcr.io/lutrarutra/codeflower-sandbox:0.38.0, downloaded on first use) |
| `--image-tag string` |  | build of the published image to use instead of 0.38.0, the release this app is made for: latest, another release (0.2.1, or 0.2 for its newest patch) or a commit (sha-abc1234) (or set $CODEFLOWER_IMAGE_TAG) |
| `-i, --input stringArray` |  | folder with your data, mounted read-only at /data/input/NAME (repeatable) |
| `--isolate-network` |  | cut the sandbox off the network except for its agents' services and the hosts in the allowlist (Linux) |
| `--jobs string` |  | let the agent ask for batch jobs, each run in a sandbox like this one: slurm, local, auto, a scheduler profile of the config, or off (default: the config's jobs.scheduler) |
| `--memory string` |  | memory the agent may use, e.g. 32G (default: the batch job's allocation; Docker and Podman also enforce it) |
| `--new-key` |  | give the project a new key and TLS certificate: links saved before no longer connect |
| `--no-tunnel` |  | keep this sandbox from browsers paired through the tunnel (it does not start the client for the tunnel either) |
| `-o, --output stringArray` |  | folder for results, created if needed and mounted read-write at /data/output/NAME (repeatable) |
| `--port int` |  | port of the worker (and its page with --server) (default: any free port); fails if it is taken |
| `-p, --project string` | `default` | project name: its sessions, logins and workspace live in ~/codeflower/projects/NAME |
| `--projects-dir string` |  | folder of the projects started with --project (or projects_dir in the config; default ~/codeflower/projects) |
| `--server` |  | also serve the chat page on the worker's port, and print a link to open it in a browser |
| `-s, --skills stringArray` |  | folder with a skill (a SKILL.md) or with skill folders, mounted read-only at /data/skills/NAME (repeatable) |
| `--state string` |  | project directory, instead of --project (created with owner-only permissions) |
| `--time-limit string` |  | time the agent has, e.g. 8h or 1-12:00:00 (default: the batch job's time limit); reported, not enforced |
